text:
rachel: Trying to follow the JS SDK quickstart with an Expo dev client (Hermes). The onboarding guide just says `import SDK from 'redwood-sdk'` and run, but the dev client crashes. Any minimal checklist for an Expo sample app?

theo: Metro often picks the ESM entry if package.json exports only set import->dist/index.mjs. That drags in Node-only bits (crypto/stream). Do you have control over metro?

rachel: I can change metro for a sample app, but we want the official sample to work out of the box for new users.

priya: For a local quickfix we usually: 1) alias the module to the CJS build in metro, 2) add getRandomValues + AbortController + web-streams polyfills at app entry, 3) set skipLibCheck in tsconfig to avoid node lib noise. Works but is a lot for a new dev.

jd: Example metro alias (tiny):```js
// metro.config.js
const path = require('path')
module.exports = { resolver: { extraNodeModules: { 'redwood-sdk$': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/index.cjs') } } }
```

rachel: That works. But onboarding friction: new devs copy/paste the quickstart and get cryptic Hermes errors (Symbol.asyncIterator, global.crypto). We should have a one-click expo sample that already wires shims.

theo: Agreed. Actionable asks for the SDK repo: 1) add a `react-native` or `main` field pointing to a RN-friendly build, 2) publish a tiny `examples/expo` sample (prebuilt with metro shims in App.js), 3) add an onboarding doc section for Expo/devclient listing minimal polyfills and metro snippet, 4) split types to avoid node:stream imports.

priya: Also propose a small script in examples: `yarn create redwood-expo` that scaffolds expo + wiring. Even a repo template would cut a ton of support noise.

jd: For now I'll add a tiny repro gist and a sandbox zip we can attach to the issue. It includes App.js with imports: `import 'react-native-get-random-values'; import 'abortcontroller-polyfill/dist/abortcontroller-polyfill-only';` and a ReadableStream shim using `web-streams-polyfill/ponyfill`.

expo-bot: FYI: Expo SDK 48+ provides `crypto.getRandomValues` in managed runtimes; devclients and older SDKs may still need polyfills. More at https://blog.expo.dev/.

rachel: I'll open the issue in the SDK repo with the repro + suggested PRs (expo example, RN entry, RN docs, split types). If anyone wants to draft the example app I'll push it to the gist and attach. Thanks! :thumbsup:
